cases.purpose: Check tty against the actual stdin terminal path, including the terminating newline, and require tty -s to return 0 without output.
cases.oracle: GNU tty and Python os.ttyname(0) on the same private slave; raw name bytes are checked before conversion to a fixed marker.
cases.comparison: Independently verified exact pathname bytes; full raw PTY output has only the verifier/status markers, so silent mode cannot emit unnoticed bytes.
cases.script:
tty > name; first=$?
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,pathlib;assert pathlib.Path("name").read_bytes()==os.fsencode(os.ttyname(0))+bytes([10]);print("name=exact")' || exit 90
rm -f name
tty -s; quiet=$?; printf "status=%s,%s\n" "$first" "$quiet"

cases.purpose: Observe the status and diagnostic after an ENOSPC write and verify output from the same shell afterwards.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear for the continued shell output; trusted setup independently proves the guest /dev/full produces ENOSPC. The bash-os status and diagnostic follow docs/clear.md.
cases.comparison: Deliberate difference: on an output error bash-os clear keeps exit status 1 and reports it with a Bash write-error diagnostic (docs/clear.md), where ncurses clear exits 0 and prints nothing. The reference side must observe status 0 and an empty diagnostic; the candidate side must observe status 1 and exactly one line ending in "clear: write error: No space left on device". Each side prints one verdict line, and the raw status and diagnostic are retained outside the compared tree. Continued shell output, the case status and the file tree are compared byte for byte with ncurses.
cases.reference_script:
clear -T xterm-256color > /dev/full 2> "$HOME/clear.diagnostic"; rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$rc" > "$HOME/clear.status"
if [[ $rc == 0 && ! -s $HOME/clear.diagnostic ]]; then printf 'output-error=as-recorded\n'; else printf 'output-error=not-as-recorded\n'; fi
printf 'recovered\n'
cases.candidate_script:
clear -T xterm-256color > /dev/full 2> "$HOME/clear.diagnostic"; rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$rc" > "$HOME/clear.status"
mapfile -t d0 < "$HOME/clear.diagnostic"
if [[ $rc == 1 && ${#d0[@]} == 1 && ${d0[0]} == *": clear: write error: No space left on device" ]]; then printf 'output-error=as-recorded\n'; else printf 'output-error=not-as-recorded\n'; fi
printf 'recovered\n'

cases.purpose: Force a four-byte partial clear write at a 1024-byte file-size limit, then EFBIG; compare status/diagnostic and shell continuation.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear -T vt100; the known ESC[H ESC[J sequence crosses the file-size limit after four bytes. Bash ignores SIGXFSZ for this bounded child shell. The bash-os status and diagnostic follow docs/clear.md.
cases.comparison: Deliberate difference: on an output error bash-os clear keeps exit status 1 and reports it with a Bash write-error diagnostic (docs/clear.md), where ncurses clear exits 0 and prints nothing. The reference side must observe status 0 and an empty diagnostic; the candidate side must observe status 1 and exactly one line ending in "clear: write error: File too large". Each side prints one verdict line, and the raw status and diagnostic are retained outside the compared tree. The resulting 1024 bytes are exact and compared with ncurses, as are the subsequent output and the file tree; the size limit is confined to the disposable subshell.
cases.reference_script:
(
trap "" XFSZ; ulimit -f 1
clear -T vt100 >> short.out 2> "$HOME/clear.diagnostic"; rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$rc" > "$HOME/clear.status"
if [[ $rc == 0 && ! -s $HOME/clear.diagnostic ]]; then printf 'output-error=as-recorded\n'; else printf 'output-error=not-as-recorded\n'; fi
printf 'recovered\n'
)
cases.candidate_script:

cases.purpose: Run clear with stdout on a hung-up PTY (verified EIO), then restore stdout and print from the same shell.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear on an independently created private PTY; Python verifies EIO before either implementation runs. The bash-os status and diagnostic follow docs/clear.md.
cases.comparison: Deliberate difference: on an output error bash-os clear keeps exit status 1 and reports it with a Bash write-error diagnostic (docs/clear.md), where ncurses clear exits 0 and prints nothing. The reference side must record status 0 and no diagnostic; the candidate side must record status 1 and exactly one line ending in "clear: write error: Input/output error". Each side prints one verdict line, and the raw status and diagnostic are retained outside the compared tree. The recovery file, compared with ncurses and with its exact bytes, proves the invoking shell continues after restoring its output.

files.hungup.py:
import errno,os,subprocess,sys
# Usage: hungup.py SHELL STATUS [DIAGNOSTIC]. STATUS and DIAGNOSTIC are what this
# side's clear is recorded to report for a write to a hung-up terminal: the exit
# status, and the text its single diagnostic line must end with (none: silence).
home=os.environ["HOME"]
want=sys.argv[2]+"\n"
suffix=sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv)>3 else None
master,slave=os.openpty();os.close(master)
try:
 try: os.write(slave,b"probe")
 except OSError as e: assert e.errno==errno.EIO
 else: raise AssertionError("closed PTY accepted a byte")
 script='clear -T xterm-256color; rc=$?; printf "%s\\n" "$rc" > "$HOME/clear.status"; exec 1>recovery; printf "recovered\\n"'
 run=subprocess.run([sys.argv[1],"--noprofile","--norc","-c",script],stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=slave,stderr=subprocess.PIPE,timeout=5)
 open(home+"/clear.diagnostic","wb").write(run.stderr)
 lines=run.stderr.decode("utf-8","replace").splitlines()
 status=open(home+"/clear.status").read()
 ok=status==want and (lines==[] if suffix is None else len(lines)==1 and lines[0].endswith(": "+suffix))
 print("output-error=as-recorded" if ok else "output-error=not-as-recorded")
 sys.exit(run.returncode)
finally: os.close(slave)
